content: Walter Walt Dawson, born on April 26, 1982, in Portland, Oregon, is a prominent advocate for Alzheimer's disease awareness and reform. He is the son of Cecil Dawson, a British immigrant, and Clara Dawson, a native of Oregon. As a child, Dawson gained national attention through a letter-writing campaign aimed at raising awareness about Alzheimer's disease, inspired by his father’s struggle with the condition. This campaign highlighted the financial and emotional toll the disease took on his family and others in similar situations. In 1992, at the age of 9, Dawson became a national spokesperson for the Alzheimer's Association. In this capacity, he traveled to Washington, D.C., multiple times to share his family’s experiences with Alzheimer's disease before committees in both the United States Senate and the House of Representatives. During these visits, Dawson had the opportunity to meet with high-ranking officials, including President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore, to advocate for health care reform and support for families affected by Alzheimer's. Dawson’s advocacy began when the financial burden of his father’s long-term care placed his family in a precarious situation. His letter-writing campaign gained traction when he read one of his letters on National Public Radio (NPR), which became the first major media outlet to support his cause. Following this, major networks such as NBC, CBS, and Nickelodeon covered Dawson’s efforts, bringing national attention to the struggles faced by families dealing with Alzheimer’s disease and the need for health care reform. As he grew older, Dawson remained committed to his advocacy work. While studying as an undergraduate at the University of Portland, he was elected Student Body Vice-President and served as President of the Student Senate. After completing his undergraduate studies, Dawson joined AmeriCorps for a year of service before pursuing further education in England. He studied at the London School of Economics and, in the fall of 2007, began a postgraduate degree in Comparative Health Policy at Oxford University.
